ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $OC\perp AB$ at point $O$, $\angle COD=\frac{1}{4}\angle BOD$, and $OE$ bisects $\angle BOD$. A ray $OF$ is drawn through point $O$, and if $OF\perp OE$, what is the measure of $\angle BOF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
Solution: As shown in the figure, when OF is above line AB,

$\because$ OF$\perp$OE,

$\therefore$ $\angle EOF=90^\circ$,

$\because$ $\angle BOE=60^\circ$,

$\therefore$ $\angle BOF=\angle BOE+\angle EOF=60^\circ+90^\circ=150^\circ$;

When OF is below line AB,

$\because$ OF$\perp$OE,

$\therefore$ $\angle EOF=90^\circ$,

$\because$ $\angle BOE=60^\circ$,

$\therefore$ $\angle BOF=\angle EOF-\angle BOE=90^\circ-60^\circ=\boxed{30^\circ}$,

Therefore, the measure of $\angle BOF$ is $150^\circ$ or $\boxed{30^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the figure: in the attached figure, AB is a horizontal straight line, O is on AB, A is on the left side, and B is on the right side; OC goes vertically upward from O, so OC is perpendicular to AB; OD points from O to the upper left, OE points from O to the upper right, and OF is not drawn in the figure. Then reason: let x=∠COD, y=∠BOD. From the positions of the rays in the figure, ∠BOD=∠BOC+∠COD; also because OC⊥AB, and OB is on AB, ∠BOC=90°. The problem gives ∠COD=1/4∠BOD, that is, x=y/4, so y=90°+y/4, solving gives 3y/4=90°, so y=120°. OE bisects ∠BOD, so ∠BOE=120°/2=60°. Also OF⊥OE, so ∠EOF=90°. Since the ray OF passing through O and perpendicular to OE has two possible directions: if OF is above AB and biased to the left, then ∠BOF=∠BOE+∠EOF=60°+90°=150°; if OF is below AB and biased to the right, then ∠BOF=|90°-60°|=30°.
